question: Should `scripts/check-workflows.mjs` apply the new fixed five-minute failure boundary to every supported workflow-check subprocess?
rationale: The implementation and proof support bounded termination, but choosing a global hard cap changes behavior for existing slow environments and is an operational policy decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the fixed five-minute bound
options.body: Merge after rebase/check refresh, accepting that unusually slow workflow checks now fail with a diagnostic instead of waiting indefinitely.

options.title: Narrow the timeout scope
options.body: Limit the timeout to known externally hanging commands if maintainers need to preserve unlimited execution for another supported check path.

options.title: Pause for workflow-budget evidence
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers cannot yet confirm that all supported environments complete these checks within five minutes.

recommendation.title: Accept the fixed five-minute bound
recommendation.body: Merge after rebase/check refresh, accepting that unusually slow workflow checks now fail with a diagnostic instead of waiting indefinitely.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence fallback routing candidate for a repository-level scripts policy decision.
